# Exact directional three-fiber budget frontier and its mismatch reserve

This note keeps the common continuous normal throughout. It provides an
attained scalar frontier, with its saturation branches, and an exact
planar formula for the reserve created by different component zero
locations. It makes no claim that these directional frontiers have a
common point at the OC budget.

## 1. The actual directional profile

Let A,K,R be full-dimensional compact convex d-bodies with
(A+R)/2 subset K. Put a=|A|, b=|K|, r=|R|, m=min(a,r),
and D=(A+R)/2. Fix a unit vector u. Write

    F(s)=|K intersect {u.x>=s}|,
    P(s)=inf_t [|A intersect {u.x>=s+t}|
                         +|R intersect {u.x>=s-t}|],
    G(s)=F(s)+P(s).

Then G(u.g) is the exact minimum over all ambient through-(0,g)
caps with this continuous normal. Both endpoint traces use the same
integer coefficient t. Purely integer caps have masses b+a and b+r
and are retained separately when taking the full directional infimum.

Let l_K=min_K u.x and h_K=max_K u.x. The ordinary profile F is
continuous and strictly decreasing on [l_K,h_K]. The two-layer
quantile theorem in `candidate 0fcbc670d417c3ed`
proves that P is continuous and nonincreasing, ranges from m to zero,
and has an inverse threshold Q(p) for 0<=p<m. Here Q(0)=h_D(u).
Its left plateau starts at the finite limiting threshold Q(m-).
Moreover Q(m-)>=l_D(u)>=l_K: every endpoint quantile is bounded
below by its endpoint lower support, and the weighted average is
bounded below by l_D(u). Also h_D(u)<=h_K by compatibility.

Consequently

    G(l_K)=b+m, G(h_K)=0,

and G is continuous and strictly decreasing on this entire interval.
Thus, for each 0<B<b+m, there is one and only one threshold s_B in
(l_K,h_K) with G(s_B)=B. For candidate g in K the directional
depth condition G(u.g)>=B is exactly the closed halfspace condition

    u.g<=s_B.                                        (1)

This is an ordinary halfspace cut in the candidate center, not a
claim of root concavity in the budget.

## 2. An attained allocation formula, including full and empty caps

For 0<=k<b define q(k) to be the threshold satisfying F(q(k))=k,
with q(0)=h_K. At full mass define the extended threshold

    q(b)=-infinity.

For 0<=p<m let Q(p) be the inverse paired threshold from Section 1;
at full pair mass set

    Q(m)=-infinity.

These full-mass conventions record the exact conditions

    F(s)<=k iff s>=q(k),
    P(s)<=p iff s>=Q(p),                              (2)

including that F(s)<=b and P(s)<=m impose no lower threshold.
They are deliberately different from the finite endpoint values of
the proper cap quantiles.

The exact formula is

    s_B = min_(k+p=B, 0<=k<=b, 0<=p<=m)
                          max{q(k),Q(p)}.             (3)

Every feasible allocation in (3) gives G(s)<=B whenever s is at
least its displayed maximum. Thus its maximum is at least s_B.
Conversely set k=F(s_B) and p=P(s_B). This is a feasible allocation.
Since s_B lies strictly inside the projection interval, 0<k<b and
q(k)=s_B. If p<m, Q(p)<=s_B by (2); if p=m this follows from the
extended convention. Hence this allocation attains exactly s_B.
This proves both equality and attainment without a compactness
argument for discontinuous extended endpoint values.

For B<m and B<b, no full-cap branch is present. In that case q(B-p)
is increasing in p and Q(p) is decreasing. Formula (3) is the
minimum of the maximum of these two functions on 0<=p<=B. It is
at their unique crossing when there is a crossing, and otherwise at
the appropriate endpoint. The exact saturated branch p=m uses
q(B-m) when feasible. The formula itself, rather than an informal
continuation of the proper quantiles, decides which branch occurs.

The two individual root-quantile profiles are concave, as established
by ordinary cap Brunn--Minkowski and the two-layer theorem. The
maximum in (3) does not preserve their concavity. The following
calculation identifies this failure and a positive reserve precisely.

## 3. The exact curvature identity for component roots

On an open interval suppose F(s)=f(s)^d and P(s)=p(s)^d, where
f,p are positive twice continuously differentiable functions. Put
W=F+P. Differentiating twice gives the identity

    (W^(1/d))''
      =W^(1/d-2) [
          W(f^(d-1) f''+p^(d-1) p'')
          +(d-1) f^(d-2) p^(d-2) (f p'-p f')^2
        ].                                            (4)

To verify (4), use W'=d(f^(d-1)f'+p^(d-1)p') and
W''=d(f^(d-1)f''+p^(d-1)p'')
+d(d-1)(f^(d-2)f'^2+p^(d-2)p'^2). The cross-term identity is

    W(f^(d-2)f'^2+p^(d-2)p'^2)
       -(f^(d-1)f'+p^(d-1)p')^2
       =f^(d-2)p^(d-2)(f p'-p f')^2.

Thus concavity of both component roots does not settle the sign:
the second term in (4) is nonnegative and measures their different
relative slopes. This identity does not infer any differentiability
at a full/empty transition; Sections 1--2 do not require it there.

## 4. Sharp planar frustum formula

In d=2, suppose on a specified interval of proper traces the actual
profiles have the forms

    F(s)=alpha(s_0-s)^2,
    P(s)=beta(s_1-s)^2,

with alpha,beta>0 and s<min(s_0,s_1). Put

    A=alpha+beta,
    bar_s=(alpha s_0+beta s_1)/A,
    E=(alpha beta/A)(s_0-s_1)^2.

Completing the square gives the exact identity

    G(s)=A(bar_s-s)^2+E.                              (5)

On this branch its frontier is therefore

    s_B=bar_s-sqrt((B-E)/A).                          (6)

The domain is restricted to those budgets whose root lies in the
specified proper-trace interval; no branch extrapolation is made.
The additive reserve E vanishes exactly when the two profiles have
the same zero location. For E>0, the map from R=sqrt(B) to s_(R^2)
is strictly convex on this branch: differentiating (6) gives

    d^2/dR^2 s_(R^2)=E/[sqrt(A)(R^2-E)^(3/2)]>0.

So replacing the actual frontier by a concave root-quantile is
incorrect, while discarding E also discards an exact positive
contribution to every cap on the branch.

## 5. Realization by an actual nonheavy three-fiber source

The source in
`candidate 4c55389e587862a0`
provides exact proper profiles realizing (5), without hypothetical
scalar tails. It has d=2,

    T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}, delta=1/8,
    A=T, R=2T,
    K=(-delta,-delta)+(7/4)T.

Its actual compatibility is (A+R)/2=(3/2)T subset K, and its fiber
areas are 1/2,49/32,2, all strictly below half their sum 129/32.
Use the linear coordinate v.x=-(x_1+x_2), without unit normalization;
rescaling u only rescales the thresholds and does not change cap mass.
For s=-2t with 0<t<=1/3 the exact endpoint optimized profile is

    P(s)=s^2,

and the middle profile is

    F(s)=(1/2)(1/4-s)^2.

For completeness, both endpoint fibers contain the simplex 3tT
with centroid (t,t). The proved paired-centroid-tail inequality
therefore gives endpoint mass at least 4t^2 for every tilt, and
the zero-tilt cap x_1+x_2<=2t attains 4t^2. The middle trace of
this cap is a triangle of area 2(t+delta)^2, proving the displayed
F. Thus the two formulas use actual cap masses throughout the
specified branch.

Here A=3/2, bar_s=1/12, E=1/48, so

    G(s)=(3/2)(s-1/12)^2+1/48,
    s_B=1/12-sqrt((2/3)(B-1/48)).                     (7)

For example, s=-1/4 gives G(s)=3/16 exactly. Formula (7) keeps
the nonzero mismatch reserve of 1/48. The source already has a
separately verified OC-safe point; this computation neither gives
an OC obstruction nor claims a full-dimensional center selection.
